title: Tuason v. Register of Deeds
respondent: Register of Deeds of Caloocan City
summary: The Supreme Court upheld the indefeasibility of a Torrens title, ruling that a certificate of title is conclusive evidence of ownership and cannot be collaterally attacked. The Torrens system was established to quiet title and guarantee the integrity of land titles.
doctrine: A Torrens certificate of title is indefeasible and imprescriptible. It cannot be altered, modified, or cancelled except in a direct proceeding. The purpose of the Torrens system is to guarantee the integrity of land titles and to protect the holder in good faith from any claim except those noted on the certificate.
fullText:
CONCEPCION, C.J.:

The central issue is the indefeasibility of a Torrens title registered under Act No. 496.

The Torrens system was adopted in the Philippines to quiet title to land and to put a stop forever to any question of the legality of the title. Once a title is registered under the Torrens system, the owner may rest secure, without the necessity of waiting in the portals of the court to avoid the possibility of losing his land.

A certificate of title serves as evidence of an indefeasible and incontrovertible title to the property in favor of the person whose name appears therein. After the expiration of one year from the issuance of the decree of registration, the title becomes conclusive and indefeasible.
